title: Incident writeup (Drive): Console auth outage after session cookie hardening
body:
Context
This is the detailed writeup for the 2026-03-10 customer-impacting outage in Redwood Console login. We did not copy this into Confluence; this Drive doc is the source of truth per the Console team's incident process.

Customer impact
- Yes. Console users were intermittently unable to sign in (looping redirect or blank page).
- Duration: ~41 minutes (highest impact), with residual issues for ~15 minutes due to browser caching.
- Affected surface: console.redwoodinference.com (hosted).

Owning engineering team
- Platform Engineering (Console & Identity)

Timeline (UTC)
- 21:02 Alert: console_login_success_rate < 90%
- 21:06 Confirmed user reports + synthetic checks failing
- 21:11 Suspected cookie attribute change deployed earlier (SameSite + Secure)
- 21:18 Rolled back the console-web release
- 21:23 Login success improves but not fully
- 21:31 Purged CDN cache for /auth/callback path
- 21:43 Back to baseline

Root cause
A security hardening change set a stricter session cookie attribute combination. In Safari and some embedded browsers, the callback flow dropped the cookie when redirected via our auth subdomain, causing an infinite login loop. CDN caching of the callback page extended the blast radius after rollback.

Action items
- Add browser matrix canary for auth callback (Owner: Console team; Due 2026-03-31)
- Add incident guardrail: block deploy if login synthetic check fails in staging (Owner: Release Eng; Due 2026-04-10)
- Document CDN cache purge steps in Console on-call runbook (Owner: SRE; Due 2026-03-25)

Notes
We consider this a customer-impacting incident writeup equivalent to a postmortem for the purpose of incident accounting.
